.... Complainant
(By the learned Public Prosecutor)
AND Bhaskar Hegde,

S/o.Late Narayana Hegde,
Aged about 44 years,
R/at No.236, C/o.Shivanna's house,
Ist Main road,
Srinivas Nagar,
Sunkadakatte,
Bengaluru-91.

.... ACCUSED  (By Sri PC, Advocate)
 2 S.C.No.1443/2023  * * * * *
 J U D G M E N T

The PSI has submitted charge sheet against the accused for the offence punishable U/s.498A, 341,
326, 307, 201, 504, 506 of IPC in Crime No.213/2023 of Kamakshipalya P.S.
2.

The brief story of the prosecution are as under:
Kamakshipalya P.S vs Bhaskar Hegde on 6 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/42840036/
1
That the accused and complainant loved each other and married on 01.02.2008 in Ganesha temple, 19 th cross, Pipeline road, Muthuraya swamy layout, Sunkadakatte.

Later accused in intoxication conditions used to quarrel with C.W.1 and children and subjected her to physical and mental cruelty, at house No.236, 1st Main road,
Srinivas Nagar, Sunkadakatte, within the limits of Kamakshipalya police station.

On 27.05.2023 at 8.00 p.m accused in intoxication condition quarrelled with C.W.1 and attempted to assault his son, when C.W.1 came to rescue her son, accused attempted to assaulted C.W.1 with knife, when C.W.1 came near the passage, the accused with an intention to kill the complainant and attempted to assault the C.W.1 on her neck,
perhaps C.W.1 kept her left hand to protect herself, due to which she sustained bleeding injuries and accused in order to screen the offence of assault, washed the blood stained knife with water and thereby the accused has committed the offences as alleged against him.
3. The concerned police have submitted charge sheet before the concerned ACMM., Bangalore.
The learned Magistrate has took cognizance of the offences and committed the case to the Sessions Court by complying Sec.207 of Cr.P.C. after furnishing copy of charge sheet to the accused.

The same was numbered as SC No.1443/2023.
4.
The prosecution has examined eleven witnesses as PW.1 to PW.11 and got exhibited documents at Ex.P1 to P14 and got marked material objects at M.O.1 to M.O.3.
The witnesses C.W.3 and C.W5 remained absent before the court.
Inspite of issue of summons, bailable warrant and NBW the concerned police failed to execute the same and keep them present before the court.

As such the prayer of the learned public prosecutor was rejected and the witnesses C.W.3 and C.W.5 were dropped.
5.
The accused has pleaded not guilty.
After completion of prosecution side evidence, this Court has recorded the statement of accused, as provided U/s.313 of Cr.P.C.
The accused has denied incriminating evidence present against him and not claimed any defense evidence nor submitted anything to the Court.
The accused has complied application u/s.437A of Cr.PC by executing personal bond and surety bond.

6. Heard the arguments on both sides and perused the materials on record.
7.

The following points that arises for consideration of this court:
1. Whether the prosecution proves that accused loved C.W.1 and got married her on 01.02.2008 at Ganesha temple, 19 th cross, Pipeline road, Mutharayaswamy Layout,
Sunkadakatte, later accused consuming alcohol used to abuse C.W.1 and her children and assault them and subjected the CW.1 to mental and physical cruelty and thereby committed the offence punishable under Section 498(A) of IPC?
2. Whether the prosecution proves that accused in the said place used to abuse C.W.1 and her children and assault them and subjected the CW.1 to mental and physical Kamakshipalya P.S vs Bhaskar Hegde on 6 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/42840036/
2 cruelty and wrongfully restrained C.W.1 from proceeding further and thereby accused has committed an offence punishable U/s.341 of IPC ?

3. Whether the prosecution proves that 27.05.2023 at 8.00 p.m at said place, accused quarelling with C.W.1 and abused her and when accused attempted to assault her son, when CW.1 questioned accused, accused abused her in filthy language and thereby you accused has committed an offence punishable U/s.504 of IPC?

4. Whether the prosecution proves that on 27.05.2023 at 8.00 p.m at said place,
accused followed C.W.1 from behind and showed knife and caused criminal intimidation to her by threatening her & thereby accused has committed an offence punishable under Section 506 of IPC?
5. Whether the prosecution proves that on 27.05.2023 at 8.00 p.m at said place,
accused attempted to assault on the neck of C.W.1, when C.W.1 tried to escape and gave her left hand to obstruct, her left hand caused bleeding injuries and thereby accused committed an offence punishable U/s.326 of IPC?
6.

Whether the prosecution proves that 27.05.2023 at 8.00 p.m at said place, accused with an intention and knowledge to kill C.W.1 attempted to assault on the neck of C.W.1, when C.W.1 tried to escape and gave her left hand to obstruct, her left hand caused bleeding injuries and thereby accused has committed an offence punishable U/s.307 of IPC?
7.

Whether the prosecution proves that on 27.05.2023 at 8.00 p.m at said place,
accused attempted to assault on the neck of C.W.1, when C.W.1 tried to escape and gave her left hand to obstruct, her left hand caused bleeding injuries and accused in order to destroy the evidence washed the blood stained knife with water and thereby accused has committed an offence punishable U/s.201 of IPC?
8. What order?
8. This Court has answered the above above points are as under:
 Point No.1: In the Negative  Point No.2: In the Negative  Point No.3: In the Negative  Point No.4: In the Negative  Point No.5: In the Negative  Point No.6: In the Negative  Point No.7: In the Negative  Point No.8: As per final order  for the following:
Kamakshipalya P.S vs Bhaskar Hegde on 6 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/42840036/
3  R E A S O N S 9.
Points Nos.1 to 7: These points are taken up together as they are related to each other and to avoid repetition in the discussion.

The prosecution got examined prime witness of the prosecution and victim by name Lalitha ie.
complainant as P.W.1.
Admittedly, the complainant is none other than the wife of the accused.
According to the evidence of complainant, the accused is a Tailor.

Due to the marital relationship,
they are having two children.
The further evidence of complainant reveals that the accused is in the habit of consuming liquor and used to quarrel for silly reasons.
According to the version of complainant, the accused never tried to assault with a knife and she has not taken any treatment in the hospital.
Even today, she and accused alongwith their children living happily.
Though the complaint has been marked through this witness as Ex.P.1, but it is the specific say of the complainant that the accused never tried to kill her.

The further evidence shows that the police have obtained her signatures on documents in the police station and she doesn't know the contents of Ex.P.1 and also Mahazar Ex.P.2 and failed to identify the seized M.Os present before the court.

Since the evidence of the complainant went against to the recitals of the complaint, Mahazar Ex.P.2 and prosecution story, hence learned PP has treated the said witness as hostile and cross-examined with the permission of the court by suggesting the contents of complaint and Mahazar Ex.P.2.
But the complainant has not admitted any suggestions of the learned PP.
As such the evidence of the wife of the complainant by name Lalitha not worthful to believe the allegations made against the accused.

10. The family members and relatives by name Krishna Nayak, Sunanda, Narayana, Muthunayak,
Madhavi, Mangibai, and another Kumar have been examined by the prosecution as PW.4 to P.W.9 respectively.

According to the evidence of the said witness P.W.4 to P.W.9, the accused never tortured the complainant either physically or mentally for any reasons nor abused and given threat to her life and never tried to kill the complainant by using knife.
According to these witnesses the police have not recorded their respective statements.
The said witnesses including the complainant not identified the knife present before the court.
Since the evidence of said witnesses contrary to the story of the prosecution, hence the learned PP has treated the said witnesses as hostile with the permission of the court and cross-examined.
The prosecution has failed to elicit any incriminating evidence during the cross- examination of the said witnesses to believe the allegation made against the accused.
As such the evidence by P.W.4 to P.W.9 not helpful for the prosecution to prove the guilt against the accused.
11. In this case, the prosecution examined the Doctor Basappa S.Hoogara as P.W.2.

It is very clear from the evidence of the said doctor P.W.2 that on 27.05.2023 at 9.15 p.m., the complainant Lalitha alongwith her son and sister came to hospital with history of assault caused by her husband.
He has treated the victim and issued wound certificate as per Ex.P.3.
According to the doctor, there was incised wound measuring 8cm x 0.3cm x under lying palmar structures deep present obliquely over left palm with profuse bleeding.
The said injury is grievous in nature.
The evidence of the doctor has completely denied by the accused counsel.

Kamakshipalya P.S vs Bhaskar Hegde on 6 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/42840036/
4 12.

The P.W.3 Dr.Bharathi Kodnapur, FSL Officer deposed that on 14.06.2023 the Kamakashipalya police C.W.14 produced three sealed articles for chemical examination and the same is sent for chemical examination and found that the blood stains on the three sealed articles are of human blood and the blood found on articles 2 and 3 are of 'O' group blood, the blood found on Article 1 knife cannot be grouped.
She has given report and returned the sealed articles to the police officials and got marked the knife, blood stained top and pant at M.O.1 to 3 and the report at Ex.P.4.
The evidence of the FSL Officer has completely denied by the accused counsel.
13. In this case, the prosecution examined panchas of the spot Mahazar marked at Ex.P.2.
The victim/ complainant Lalitha and pancha Narayana examined as PW.1 and P.W.6 respectively.

Both witnesses PW.1 and P.W.6 though admitted their signatures present on Ex.P.2, but it is the say of the said witnesses that the police have obtained their signatures in the police station, hence learned PP has cross-examined both PW.1 and P.W.6 treating them as hostile with the permission of the court, but both the panchas failed to admit the suggestions of the learned PP.
In the cross-examination of accused counsel, both panchas admitted that they do not know the contents of Ex.P.2 and they signed the Ex.P.2 at the request of the police.

As such the evidence placed by the prosecution related to Mahazar Ex.P.2 through witnesses P.W.1 and P.W.6 not helpful for the prosecution to prove the Mahazar Ex.P.2.
14.
It is necessary to note that the pancha by name Krishna Nayak examined as PW.4 being the signatory to the seizure Mahazar marked at Ex.P.6 also not supported the prosecution story.
According to this witness PW.4, the police have not seized the knife in his presence under Mahazar Ex.P.6 in the presence of accused.

As such the learned PP treated the said pancha P.W.4 as hostile and cross- examined, but not able to bring out any useful evidence to believe the concerned IO has carried out seizure Mahazar in his presence at the spot.

Hence the evidence given by the seizure pancha P.W.4 not worthful for the prosecution to prove the said seizure Mahazar Ex.P.6.
15.
The ASI Govinda examined as P.W.10 has deposed that on 28.05.2023 as per the instructions of C.W.15, he went to the hospital and recorded statement of C.W.1 and produced it before C.W.15.
The evidence of P.W.10 has completely denied by the accused counsel.

16. The PSI Pradeep Kumar.H.S. examined as P.W.11 has deposed that on 27.05.2023 received MLC came from Lakshmi hospital, on 28.05.2023 he deputed C.W.10 to visit hospital in view of MLC.
Accordingly, the C.W.10 went to the hospital and recorded complaint of C.W.1 in the presence of doctor and produced before him.

In view of the complaint, P.W.11 has registered FIR vide Cr.No.213/2023, on the same day he deputed CW.12 and C.W.13 to trace the accused, the said police officials traced the accused and produced before him.
He has recorded voluntary statement of the accused.
On 29.05.2023 in view of statement of accused, he went alongwith accused and C.W.4 and 5 to the place of incident and seized the knife produced by the accused.
Accordingly, prepared Mahazar Ex.P.6 and thereafter produced the accused before court alongwith remand application for judicial custody.
On 31.05.2023 he has seized the blood stained clothes marked at M.O.2 and 3 produced by victim P.W.1 in the presence of C.W.2 and C.W.3 and prepared spot Mahazar Ex.P.2.
On the same day, he received wedding card, photos and marriage registration certificate as per Ex.P.14, and wound certificate Ex.P.3.

He sent M.O.1 to 3 to FSL on 14.06.2023 and thereafter Kamakshipalya P.S vs Bhaskar Hegde on 6 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/42840036/
5 received the FSL report and he has recorded statements of witnessess and as the investigation was completed, hence submitted charge sheet against the accused.
The evidence of the Investigation Officer has completely denied by the accused counsel.

In this case, even if assumed that the said Investigation Officer has deposed evidence according to his investigation, perhaps as already discussed above, the prime witness i.e victim and all other independent witnesses including panchas turned hostile and thereby not supported the prosecution story.
So, it is very clear from the above discussions that the prosecution has completely failed to place the reliable iota evidence before the court to prove the allegations made against the accused.
As such, this court has answered the Point Nos.1 to 7 in the Negative.
17. Point No.8:

In view of answer of this court on points No.1 to 7, this court proceed to pass the following:
O R D E R U/s.235(1) of Cr.P.C. the accused is hereby acquitted of the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 341, 326, 307, 201, 504, 506 of IPC.
The bail bonds and surety bonds of accused stand cancelled.
The M.O.1 is knife being worthful shall be confiscated to State as per law after expiry of appeal time.
M.Os.2 and 3 being clothes of complainant are being worthless are ordered to be destroyed after expiry of appeal time.
